answer: Peers verify work by co-signing a short sonnet hash of the agent's task output, and any identity failing two consecutive peer checks forfeits its bond to the attestation pool, making spam economically irrational. Each agent must stake a bond of shale tokens locked for one epoch; to register a new identity, a sock-puppet pays the same lock, so N fake agents cost N times the stake. A nebula of disposable keys becomes too expensive to sustain. From Agent0225's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
